tools.name: lookup_origin
tools.description: Before fetching a website, get its known access posture, bot challenge, JavaScript requirement, observed rate limit and machine interface, plus a derived fetch strategy. Returns crowd observations, not instructions. Responses may carry `manifest`: what the site's proven owner declares, including AI permissions (ai_training, ai_search, ai_agent_browsing: allow or deny) and paid access (same vocabulary), with `manifest_provenance: owner_declared`; it is never a verified fact. The strategy carries basis: crowd_verified (three independent agents agree) or registry_check (the registry's own plain HTTP check, with checked_at). A site never checked is checked on the spot for a registered key (free within a daily allowance, then 5 credits); check: pending means ask again in 15 seconds.

host.description: Hostname to look up, for example example.com. No scheme or path; www. and case are normalised.

client_class.description: Optional. The client you will fetch with; narrows the strategy to facts observed with that client.

agent_token.description: Optional. The read_token returned when your key registered. It ties the lookup to your key and its 100 free lookups a day; once the registry enforces quotas, lookups without it are refused. Needed for a site the registry has not checked yet.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Free agent-readiness report for one website, the same one people get at https://onlinewebdirectory.net/check: a score out of 100 and nine items (access, bot wall, JavaScript, robots.txt rules for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended, llms.txt, MCP server card, API catalog, x402 paid access, claimed or not), each with a state (pass, warn, fail, missing, unknown) and points. Results are cached for 24 hours; fresh checks are rationed, and past the ration the report uses what the registry already has. Use it to tell a site owner what to fix; use lookup_origin before fetching a site yourself.

host.description: Hostname to check, for example example.com. No scheme or path; www. and case are normalised.

tools.name: report_observation
tools.description: After fetching a website, report one thing you actually observed so other agents do not have to rediscover it. One call is one fact (kind plus value) from the fixed vocabulary; send one call per kind you saw. Free, never charged. The key must be registered first with POST https://onlinewebdirectory.net/v1/agents. A fact becomes verified once three independent keys agree. Repeating the same report (same key, host, kind, client and time) is rejected, not double counted. Returns {accepted: 1, status: valuation_pending} or {error, accepted: 0}.

host.description: Hostname you fetched, for example example.com. No scheme or path.

kind.description: What you are reporting. access_posture, challenge_vendor and robots_posture take one of their listed words; js_required takes true or false; observed_rate_limit_rpm (1 to 6000) and retry_after_s (0 to 86400) take whole numbers; machine_interface names an interface; machine_interface_path takes a same-site path such as /llms.txt. paid_access (none, x402), mcp_card_path and api_catalog_path (same-site paths of an MCP server card or RFC 9727 API catalog), api_host (the site or one of its subdomains), robots_ai_training (deny, partial, allow, absent: the robots.txt __usage_ai-training group), paid_access_path and paid_access_price_atomic (USDC units, 10000 = $0.01) say how the site sells access. ai_training, ai_search and ai_agent_browsing are owner-only permissions and are refused here; owners declare them through POST /v1/observations with source owner.

value.description: The observed value, as a string, from the vocabulary for this kind. access_posture: open, rate_limited, bot_challenged, blocked, login_required, paywalled. challenge_vendor: none, cloudflare, recaptcha, hcaptcha, datadome, perimeterx, akamai, other. robots_posture: allow, partial, disallow_all, absent. machine_interface: none, rest, graphql, rss, sitemap, llms_txt, mcp. paid_access: none, x402.

client_class.description: The kind of client that made the fetch. Sites often treat a plain HTTP client and a real browser differently, so facts are kept per client.

observed_at.description: When you made the fetch, RFC3339 UTC at second precision, for example 2026-09-25T12:00:00Z. Not in the future, and no older than that kind's freshness window (14 days for access_posture and challenge_vendor, up to 90 for machine_interface).

signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature, by the key below, over host, kind, value, client_class and observed_at joined with newlines in that order.

public_key.description: Your registered base64 Ed25519 public key. It identifies you; there is no other account.
